result:
Read. Plan is 3 steps:

1. `--verbose` flag on `greet.py` → prints `verbose on` before greeting; no flag = current behaviour unchanged.
2. New `test_greet.py` — assert-based self-check of `greet()`, runs via `python3 test_greet.py`.
3. `README.md` Usage section documents `--verbose`.

Current state: `greet.py` is 9 lines, `greet(name)` returns `"hello " + name`, positional name from `sys.argv[1]` defaulting `world`. README Usage is one code line. No test file yet. So all three steps are additive, nothing to remove.

One implementation detail I'll settle when I start: `--verbose` and the positional `name` coexist, so flag has to be filtered out of argv before picking the name — otherwise `greet.py --verbose Ian` greets `--verbose`. Plan says behaviour without the flag doesn't change, so no argparse rewrite of the default path; filtering the flag out of argv keeps that true.

Standing by — say go.
